bullets.title: US-Iran military conflict drives oil above $90/bbl; Hormuz shipping severely disrupted
bullets.body: US conducted nine consecutive nights of strikes on Iranian military sites as casualties mounted (17+ US troops killed). Brent surged above $90-91/bbl—highest since June—as Iran halted Caspian Pipeline Consortium loadings, struck Kuwait's largest power plant/desalination facility, and fired on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. US crude inventories at 43-day supply, lowest in 45 years. US gas prices crossed $4/gallon. Jefferies and ROTH both flagged geopolitical risk as underpriced, with Polymarket assigning 31% odds of full US invasion of Iran by 2027.

bullets.title: Semis enter bear market (-20% from June highs); Kimi K3 triggers DeepSeek-like panic
bullets.body: The SOX fell 20%+ from late-June records—its worst week since April—as China's Moonshot AI released Kimi K3, a 2.8T-parameter open-weight model scoring near frontier proprietary models. GS data showed Info Tech was the most net-sold US sector in the past week, with cumulative HF selling since early June the largest on the 10-year record. UBS, JPM, and Citi all argue the selloff is overdone: Kimi K3 actually drives more HBM/DRAM/server DDR5 demand via Jevons' Paradox, and TSMC's CFO confirmed strong multi-year AI chip demand with $265B committed to Arizona capacity.

bullets.title: 2Q26 earnings tracking 28% EPS growth; 83-88% beat rates well above historical averages
bullets.body: With ~13% of S&P 500 market cap reported, aggregate EPS is tracking +28.3% growth (UBS) vs. 25% consensus, with 83-88% beat rates vs. the 5-year average of 78-79%. Financials lead at 95% beats; TECH+ (led by NVDA at 97% expected YoY growth) tracking 47.8% EPS expansion. Big week ahead: GOOGL, TSLA, TXN, NOW, T, INTC all report Wed-Thu, followed by MSFT, META, AAPL, AMZN next week—hyperscaler capex guidance is the single most-watched datapoint.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex approaching $870B in 2026; debt issuance surged to $194B
bullets.body: JPM estimates hyperscalers will spend ~$870B in AI capex in 2026 (+77% YoY), with GOOGL at $300B, AMZN $300B, META $200B for 2027. Hyperscaler bond issuance surged from ~$40-50B (2022) to ~$194B (2026). Chris Wood (Jefferies) warns of a bear case: $662B in off-balance-sheet data center lease commitments, circular vendor financing, and commoditized LLM pricing could trigger a capex ROIC reckoning. Citi flags anticipated US equity supply of over $1T in 2H as a headwind for tech.

bullets.title: Momentum unwind at historic pace; GS High Beta Momentum basket -32% from YTD highs
bullets.body: Momentum factor volatility hit a 45-year high (outside recessions) at 36%. Goldman's High Beta Momentum basket is down 32% from peaks and only +15% YTD vs. +60% a month ago. JPM notes HF momentum z-score at -0.7—historically correlating with +5.5% 1M and +12.3% 3M forward returns—and maintains a tactically bullish stance. Retail flows are 24% below YTD average. 22V Research recommends SPY Aug put spreads (730/690 for ~$5.80) as Mag7 bounce masks underlying weakness; SPY already below its 50-day MA.

bullets.title: Citi: Mag 7 'no longer relevant'; recommends broader AI 'growth cluster' strategy
bullets.body: Citi declared the Mag 7 framework obsolete and recommends rotating into a broader AI growth cluster. Mag 7 is lagging the S&P 500 YTD after leading for four years; retail is shifting to AI infrastructure enablers. Morgan Stanley also favors equal-weighted S&P over cap-weighted and prefers hyperscalers over semis hardware, citing better AI optionality and capex discipline narrative.

bullets.title: Single-stock implied vol at 40% (2.8x index IV); CTA thresholds broken in Nasdaq
bullets.body: Average S&P 500 single-stock IV hit 40%, which is 2.8x the index IV—the highest dispersion on record since 1995. Goldman notes CTA threshold levels have been broken in Nasdaq (key ST pivot 29,265; MT 27,441). SPX immediate risk range cited at 7,420-7,597. QQQ implied vol trades at a 9% discount to 30-day realized—historically a no-buy signal per Hedgeye.

bullets.title: TSMC raises 2026 capex ceiling to $64B+; commits $265B total to US Arizona expansion
bullets.body: TSMC CFO said the company sees 'strong multi-year' AI chip demand and is accelerating Arizona capacity, committing an additional $100B to bring total US investment to $265B. TSMC is also considering bond issuance to fund capex. ASML's NDR similarly confirmed 2028 capacity visibility and emerging value-based pricing discussions with customers. SK Hynix chairman forecast AI memory demand rising 50-60% YoY with customers requesting 60-100% more supply through 2027.

bullets.title: KOSPI circuit-breaker triggered; 1.2M Korean retail margin calls represent 45-year volatility record
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell 4-5% on the week—down ~25% from recent highs—triggering the exchange's sell-side sidecar mechanism. 1.2M retail investors received margin calls (3.4% of the adult population). Korea's stock market volatility reportedly hit an all-time high, exceeding GFC levels. Foreign investors dumped Korean equities at a record pace. Citi maintains KOSPI target 10,000 based on 5.8x forward PE (20-year low) and expects semiconductor supply/demand imbalance and +248% YoY earnings to recover.

bullets.title: Macro: Nominal GDP at 6% YoY; ISM expected to hit 55%; sticky inflation from energy spike
bullets.body: Nancy Lazar (Piper) flags nominal GDP running at 6% YoY with M2 well above pre-COVID trend and accelerating, ISM poised to hit 55%. June CPI/PPI came in tame (MS forecasts core PCE -0.08% headline, +0.17% core MoM), but Middle East energy shock now injects fresh inflation risk. The Fed is expected to stay on hold in 2026 and cut 50bps in 2027. Consumer confidence softened (PSC 5-day avg -2.6 pts to 104.6) and US gasoline at $4/gallon is pressuring low-income consumers.

bullets.title: China's Kimi K3 / Qwen3.8 signal structural AI leadership threat; Jefferies flags 9 Chinese institutions in global top 10
bullets.body: Jefferies research calls China's tech advance 'structural, not cyclical': nine of the top 10 global research institutions are Chinese, China's R&D spending ($1.03T PPP) exceeded the US in 2024, and Kimi K3 is only 5% behind Claude on intelligence benchmarks. DeepSeek normalized token volume surpassed US frontier models on OpenRouter by July 2026. Alibaba open-sourced SAIL to rival CUDA. Separately, China's CSRC signaled counter-cyclical intervention and Beijing deployed $8.9B to support domestic equities.

bullets.title: Investment banking in a 'golden age'; Q2 Wall Street beats driven by AI capital raising
bullets.body: JPMorgan Q2 beat consensus EPS by 9.8% (revenue +12.3%, IB fees +16.3%, equity underwriting +53.6%). Goldman Q2 revenue +39.5% YoY, EPS +44.6%; Global Banking and Markets +53.2%. Morgan Stanley equity trading +49%, ECM +25%. Steve Eisman flags AI investment returns and private credit as the primary economic risks, not bank credit quality. Bank margins at highest since 2023; AI-adopting banks outperforming peers on margin improvement.

bullets.title: NVIDIA builds dark fiber US network; SpaceX places $52B NVDA GB300 order with Foxconn
bullets.body: Wolfe Research confirmed NVIDIA is buying US long-haul dark fiber with up to 100-pair fiber counts to address GPU ecosystem bottlenecks—bullish for Ciena and Corning (both Outperform). Separately, SpaceX placed its first orders for 13,000 NVIDIA GB300 AI servers from Foxconn (~$52B); Japan committed $2.4B to NVIDIA Rubin chips for humanoid robotics. UBS sees NVDA and AVGO as offering best risk/reward with NVDA at ~16-18x C27E P/E growing 50-80% CAGR.

bullets.title: Oracle data-center cost overruns; credit risk hits all-time high
bullets.body: The Information reported Oracle faces multibillion-dollar data-center cost overruns and delays. Cost-of-default protection on Oracle bonds jumped to a new record. Oracle's Project Jupiter (2.45 GW New Mexico site) faces 1-2 year delay due to unresolved gas pipeline permitting. CLSA initiates ORCL at Hold with a $145 PT (15% upside), well below FactSet consensus of $250.

bullets.title: China semiconductor equipment imports bounce in June; UBS constructive on Chinese WFE names
bullets.body: China SPE imports surged 59% MoM to $3.0B in June, with YoY declines narrowing to -2% from -12%. Shanghai fabs +38% YoY and Beijing +64% YoY. Japan equipment exports ended their 8-month losing streak (+8% YoY). UBS maintains positive view on leading Chinese WFE names given improving memory capex outlook; forecasts 6.7% YoY growth in China's total WFE in 2026.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz effectively dysfunctional; insurers and logistics absorbing shock
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC declared the Hormuz Strait 'unsafe' while US operations continue, targeting tankers and immobilizing vessels. UKMTO reported vessel fires and incidents near Oman. The CPC oil loading terminal suspended operations twice following drone strikes on tankers. Polymarket cut odds of Hormuz normalizing in 2026 to 51% (from 64%). Jefferies notes the conflict is entering a more dangerous phase with UAE ports and airports named in Iranian warnings.

bullets.title: New York's data-center moratorium bill and grassroots opposition intensify AI infrastructure headwinds
bullets.body: New York's Responsible Data Center Development Act would impose a one-year moratorium on new large data center permits, awaiting the governor's decision. A Tea Party veteran is now leading 142 rallies across 42 states opposing data centers. ROTH flags 10+ state bans possible including Northeast, VA, MI, WA, OR, CA for solar/AI datacenter projects.

bullets.title: Memory pricing surging: server DRAM spot prices spike mid-July; 3Q ASP expected +21% QoQ
bullets.body: Server DRAM (64GB) spot prices have risen sharply since mid-July, widening the gap with contract prices. One analyst projects 3Q global DRAM ASP up 21% QoQ vs. TrendForce's 13-18% estimate. Data center DRAM prices are up 70% QoQ in Q1 and 40%+ in Q2. MS forecasts 25%+ like-for-like pricing from Q2 to Q3. Memory supply deficit expected to intensify through 2028. MU projected to generate $400B+ FCF through 2028 with 40%+ buyback potential.

bullets.title: Mega-cap tech historically choppy week; Google and Tesla earnings are the tape catalyst
bullets.body: Historical data shows tech returns for the Jul 20-24 week have a slight negative bias since 2000. GOOGL is the first hyperscaler reporting (Wed after close, $117B revenue/$2.87 EPS consensus); its capex guidance ($325-350B vs. $250B Street for 2027) and cloud growth will set the tone for the entire AI infrastructure complex. TSLA also reports Wednesday. TXN and INTC report Wed and Thu respectively.
